blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.
blocks.zh: 视觉-语言模型(VLMs)对机器人学习中的零镜头视频任务进度估计很有希望,然而,由于隐含的成功假设或相对的时间排名设计,现有的框架经常出现确认偏差,幻觉地出现死刑失败后的进展. 直觉催生边疆模型会倒塌成二进制成功探测器,无法捕捉出细微,非线性的进步和失败. 虽然培训后的方法可以通过明确的培训来缓解这种情况,但它们需要昂贵的实时机器人数据,并且需要每个单个基础模型进行计算强化的后培训。 为解决这些限制,我们引入了D&A(描述和评估):我们的方法将进度估计脱钩为客观的、以任务为依据的场景动态文字描述,然后是使用明确标题的评估阶段。 通过迫使VLM在打分前综合一个明确的基于文字的绝对成功定义,这个框架将评价锁定在外部的全球标准上,而不是视频的内部时限上. 经验结果显示,我们的方法校正了零发的估计数并减少了确认偏差,提供了精细的、部分的进展指标,准确惩罚未执行的处决,同时正确插入成功运行。 开发与援助纯粹是迅速的,它概括了各种任务、表现和基准——匹配或超越训练后奖励模式——及其奖励估计,从而能够有效地在下游加强学习。

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: First impressions are notoriously difficult to overcome [ 1 ] . When evaluating complex situations, humans often exhibit confirmation bias [ 2 ] , seeking and interpreting evidence that aligns with their initial hypotheses and introducing systematic errors into judgment. Similar biases appear in language models, which, trained to appear competent to human evaluators, distort answers to agree with users or take “shortcuts” to appear to solve given tasks [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 ] . Crucially, the psychology literature shows such biases can be mitigated through structured procedures that mandate a comprehensive description of the available data before any task assessment [ 9 , 10 ] .
blocks.zh: 第一印象难于克服 在评价复杂情况时,人类往往表现出确认偏差[2],寻求和解释符合其最初假设的证据,并将系统性错误引入判断. 类似的偏见也出现在语言模型中,这些模型受过培训,似乎能够胜任人类评估人员,扭曲答案,同意使用者的意见,或采取“捷径”似乎可以解决给定的任务[3、4、5、6、7、8]。 关键的是,心理学文献表明,这种偏见可以通过结构化的程序得到缓解,这种程序要求在进行任何任务评估之前全面描述现有数据[9、10]。

blocks.en: We build on this intuition to design better robotics reward models for downstream applications, e.g., real-world reinforcement learning and failure explanation. When naïvely querying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for zero-shot video reward estimation, we observe these same confirmation-bias shortcuts: the models frequently hallucinate progress even when little to no meaningful advancement has occurred (see Fig. 1 ). Current zero-shot robotics reward models fall victim to the same issue—frameworks like GVL [ 11 ] and TOPReward [ 12 ] estimate progress by ranking shuffled video frames or tracking token logits—our experiments show that these approaches bias towards task success. For downstream reinforcement or imitation learning algorithms, these erroneous evaluations become highly misleading reward signals that severely impede policy learning.
blocks.zh: 我们利用这种直觉来设计更好的机器人奖励下游应用的模型,例如现实世界的强化学习和失败解释. 当天真地询问Visual-Langage Models(VLMs)对零镜头视频奖励估计时,我们观察到这些相同的确认-比斯快捷键:即使几乎没有有意义的进展,这些模型也经常产生幻觉(见图1)。 目前零射出机器人奖励模型成为同一问题框架的受害者,例如GVL[11]和TOPREWORD[12]通过对被打乱的视频帧或跟踪信号记录进行排名来估计进度——我们的实验表明,这些方法偏向于任务的成功。 对于下游强化或模仿学习算法来说,这些错误的评价成为了高度误导性的奖励信号,严重阻碍了政策学习.

blocks.en: To bypass the limitations of zero-shot foundation models, recent approaches post-train models on task-specific robotic datasets [ 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] . Yet diverse real-world robotics data, with labeled failures, is hard to obtain [ 17 ] , limiting the generalization capabilities of the resulting models. Post-training is further limited to smaller, less capable open-source models and must be repeated for each individual base VLM, creating a cost, compute, and capability barrier to truly generalist robotics reward models.
blocks.zh: 为了绕过零射入地基模型的局限性,近期在任务特定的机器人数据集上接近了火车后模型[13,14,15,16]. 然而,具有被贴上标签的故障的多元现实世界机器人数据却难以获得[17],限制了由此而来模型的通化能力. 后训练进一步限于更小,能力更弱的开源模型,必须针对每个基站VLM重复使用,形成成本,计算,能力等障碍,真正通用的机器人奖赏模型.

blocks.en:
Instead, we propose D&A ( D escribe & A ssess), a zero-shot reward model that avoids the bias issues of prior zero-shot methods while achieving better visual and semantic generalization than post-trained reward models.
Being zero-shot is central to its effectiveness: requiring no robotics-specific training, the same prompt-based recipe drops directly onto any promptable VLM and improves for free as the underlying models advance.
D&A decouples evaluation into two distinct stages, description and assessment .
It first forces the VLM to generate an explicit, textual description of what the robot actually did, inducing an objective foundation for progress measurement.
It then assesses progress by reasoning about what task success means semantically and anchoring its reward estimate to the success criterion.
Conditioned on the trajectory description and this success reasoning, the VLM predicts progress over key frames in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] as dense rewards for policy learning.
We further show that this paradigm can be easily adapted to generate rich natural language feedback that goes beyond binary reward signals and provides targeted corrective context for policy improvement.
blocks.zh:
取而代之的是,我们提出D&A(Dexit & A sess),这是一种零发奖赏模式,它避免了先前零发奖方法的偏差问题,同时实现了比训练后奖赏模式更好的视觉和语义概括.
零射是其有效性的关键:不需要针对机器人的训练,同样的即时食谱会直接投入任何可迅速的VLM并随着基本模型的推进而免费改进.
D&A将评价分为两个不同的阶段:描述和评估。
它首先迫使VLM对机器人的实际行为产生清晰的文字描述,为进度测量引出客观的基础.
然后,它通过推理来评估进展,说明任务的成功意味着什么,并将其奖励估计数固定在成功标准上。
根据轨迹描述和这一成功推理,VLM预测[0, 1] [0, 1] 关键框架的进展是政策学习的密集奖励.
我们进一步表明,这种范式可以很容易地加以调整,产生超出二进制奖励信号的丰富的自然语言反馈,并为改进政策提供有针对性的纠正环境。

blocks.en:
In summary, D&A is a reward model paradigm that decouples video description from progress assessment, enabling zero-shot robotics reward modeling with pre-trained VLMs.
Because it is purely prompt-based, D&A is model-agnostic and requires no robotics data or fine-tuning; it generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and language, matching or outperforming post-trained models on reward benchmarks. Our scaling experiments show D&A improves with VLM capability across four model families and 28 open- and closed-source models.
On real-world online and offline reinforcement learning with a DROID Franka and two bimanual YAM arm tasks, D&A improves success rate over both zero-shot and post-trained reward models by + 95 % +95\% , + 15 % +15\% , and + 45 % +45\% , respectively. Finally, scaling up D&A to GPT-6 Astra achieves SOTA performance on D&A-Bench , RBM-EVAL-OOD , and RoboRewardBenchmark , surpassing all seven pre-trained and zero-shot baselines.
blocks.zh:
简而言之,D&A是一种奖励模型范式,可以将视频描述与进度评估脱钩,使零镜头机器人能够以预先训练的VLM奖励模型.
由于它纯粹是即时的,所以D&A是模型不可知的,不需要机器人数据或微调;它概括了各种任务、表现和语言,在奖励基准上匹配或优于训练后的模型。 我们的分级实验显示,在四个模组家庭和28个开源和闭源模型中,通过VLM能力,D&A得到了改进。
在现实世界在线和离线强化学习中,通过DROID Franka和两个双人YAM臂任务,D&A分别以+95%+95+,+15%+15+和+45%+45++提高零射和后训练奖励模式的成功率. 最后,将D&A扩大至GPT-6 Astra在D&A-Bench,RBM-EVAL-OOD,和RoboReward Benchmark上实现了SOTA的性能,超过了所有7个经过预训和零镜头的基线.

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Foundation models as reward models. LLMs and VLMs have been widely used to specify rewards, e.g., by generating executable reward code or shaping terms from natural language [ 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 ] , but such methods typically assume access to privileged low-dimensional state that is unavailable in real-world deployment.
A more deployable alternative uses pre-trained VLMs as zero-shot progress or success estimators directly from pixels [ 22 , 23 , 24 , 11 , 12 , 25 ] .
D&A belongs to this zero-shot family, but whereas prior methods extract a scalar signal directly—e.g., ranking shuffled frames in GVL [ 11 ] or reading the logit of a “True” token in TOPReward [ 12 ] —we route reward estimation through explicit description and assess phases, which we find essential for countering the success bias of direct prompting.
blocks.zh:
基金会模式作为奖励模式. LLMs和VLM被广泛用于指定奖励,例如通过生成可执行奖励代码或从自然语言中塑造术语[18,19,20,21],但这种方法通常假定可获得在现实世界部署中没有的特权低维状态.
更可部署的替代品使用预先训练的VLM作为从像素直接得到的零射入或成功估计器[22,23,24,11,12,25].
D&A属于这个"零射出"家族,但之前的方法直接提取出一个分级信号——例如,在GVL [11]中排出分级框,或者在TOPREWard [12]中读取"True"指号的对数——我们通过明确的描述和评估阶段进行路线奖励估计,我们认为这对于消除直接提示的成功偏差至关重要.

blocks.en:
Post-trained reward models. To improve reliability, a growing line of work fine-tunes VLMs and VLAs on robotics data with progress-prediction objectives [ 13 , 15 , 16 , 14 , 26 , 27 , 28 ] or language reasoning [ 29 , 30 ] .
RoboReward [ 15 ] predicts discretized progress labels obtained via counterfactual instruction relabeling, while Robometer [ 16 ] jointly predicts progress, success, and trajectory preferences from a large curated dataset.
These models inherit the cost of collecting diverse, high-quality robot data [ 17 ] , are restricted to open-source backbones, and must be retrained as stronger base models appear.
D&A instead remains fully zero-shot, making it model-agnostic and improving with frontier VLM improvements, while matching or exceeding post-trained models on out-of-distribution benchmarks.
blocks.zh:
后训练有素的奖励模式. 为了提高可靠性,越来越多的工作线对机器人数据的VLM和VLA进行了微调,并设定了进度预测目标[13,15,16,14,26,27,28]或语言推理[29,30].
Robo Reward [15] 预言通过反事实指令再贴标签获得的盘回化进度标签,而Robolecommed [16] 联合预言从一大型被整理的数据集获得的进展,成功和轨迹偏好.
这些模型继承了收集多样,高品质的机器人数据的成本[17],仅限于开源骨干,随着更强大的基础模型的出现,必须进行再培训.
相反,D&A仍然是完全零射出,使它成为模型不可知并随着前沿VLM改进而得到改进,同时在分配外基准上匹配或超过经过培训后的模式.

blocks.en: III Demonstrating Bias in Zero-Shot VLM Prompting
blocks.zh: 三. 以 " 零射 " 甚高频显示偏见 提示

blocks.en: Fig. 2 : Example reasoning trace generated by GPT-5.3 (queried April 11, 2026) for the opposite instruction “unfold the shirt.”
blocks.zh: 图2:GPT-5.3(2026年4月11日发出命令)为相反指示“将衬衫翻开。 “

blocks.en:
We begin with a qualitative example showing that directly prompting a zero-shot VLM [ 31 ] for per-frame progress—conditioned on a robot video and its task instruction—fails to produce accurate rewards.
Given an expert demonstration paired with the correct instruction, VLMs generally produce reasonable per-frame [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] rewards that end at 1.0 1.0 .
However, when the robot performs the task incorrectly or suboptimally, they often “shortcut” by assuming success—precisely the case a reward model must detect to correct a deployed policy.
blocks.zh:
我们首先举一个定性例子,说明在机器人录像及其任务指示的基础上,直接为每帧进展发出零射VLM[31],未能产生准确的回报。
由于专家演示与正确指示配对, VLMs 通常产生合理的每帧[0, 1] [0,1] 分出以1.0.0.
然而,当机器人不正确或不理想地完成任务时,他们往往通过假定成功而 " 缩短 " 时间——确切地说,奖励模式必须发现,以纠正已部署的政策。

blocks.en:
For example, in Fig. 2 we prompt GPT-5.3 with “provide per-timestep rewards for this video of a robot ‘unfolding the shirt’.” However, the video (from the π 0 \pi_{0} -FAST blog [ 32 ] ) in fact shows a π 0 \pi_{0} policy folding a shirt.
Rather than reasoning about task completion, the model writes a reward function that scores normalized mean pixel differences between consecutive frames, rewarding motion rather than progress.
This reflects a confirmation bias arising from fine-tuning on human feedback, which makes models unlikely to challenge user assumptions [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 ] .
blocks.zh:
例如,在图2中,我们鼓励GPT-5.3“为这个机器人`脱下衬衫'的视频提供时常奖励”。 然而,视频(取自 ^0\pi_{0}-FAST博客[32])实际上显示有 ^0\pi_{0}政策折叠衬衫.
该模型不是对任务完成的推理,而是写出一个奖励函数,将连续帧之间的平均像素差异归正,奖励运动而不是进步.
这反映了对人反馈的微调所产生的确认偏差,这使得模型不太可能挑战用户的假设[3,4,5,6,7,8].

blocks.en:
While prompt engineering can mitigate specific cases, our experiments ( Sec. V ) show that existing zero-shot reward methods—built on both closed- and open-source VLMs with custom prompting and reward-extraction schemes—still perform poorly across benchmarks, real-world tasks, and embodiments.
Next, we detail our solution: decoupled description and assessment phases.
blocks.zh:
虽然即时工程可以减轻具体的情况,但我们的实验(第5节)表明,现有的零发奖励方法——既采用封闭式的也采用开源式的VLM, 并且有定制的促发和取回奖励办法——在基准、现实世界的任务和表现方面仍然表现不佳。
其次,我们详细介绍了我们的解决办法:解开描述和评估阶段。

blocks.en:
Method Overview. We would like to directly use pre-trained VLMs, zero-shot, for reward prediction; doing so allows us to leverage the generalization capabilities and learned reasoning chains of ever-improving frontier VLMs trained on internet-scale data, all without the tedium of robotics-specific post-training.
But in practice, as demonstrated in Sec. III , we find that naïvely instantiating R ( o 1 : T , l ) R(o_{1:T},l) as a VLM suffers from confirmation bias, where the model predicts increasing rewards regardless of whether the observation-language pairing represents a success or failure.
To address these limitations, we propose Describe and Assess (D&A), which decomposes R R into two components with an explicit natural-language interface: Describer d 1 : T = D ( o 1 : T ) , ⊳ ​ Describes observed behavior in language Assessor r 1 : T = A ( l , d 1 : T ) . ⊳ ​ Scores behavior against description \begin{array}[]{lll}\text{Describer}&d_{1:T}=D(o_{1:T}),&\color[rgb]{0.5,0.5,0.5}{\vartriangleright\text{Describes observed behavior in language}}\\
\text{Assessor}&r_{1:T}=A(l,d_{1:T}).&\color[rgb]{0.5,0.5,0.5}{\vartriangleright\text{Scores behavior against description}}\\
\end{array} (1) Both functions can use the same VLM (or another function with the same specification) but are specified by different inputs and prompts and have no shared context. Each function has a specific task to help prevent inherent VLM biases that can contaminate reward generation.
The full reward function is the composition R ( o 1 : T , l ) = A ( l , D ( o 1 : T ) ) R(o_{1:T},l)=A\big(l,\,D(o_{1:T})\big) .
While we use o 1 : T o_{1:T} notation here, in practice, we linearly downsample the T T frames to H H frames with H ≪ T H\ll T , e.g., H = 8 H=8 , and then linearly interpolate the rewards to length T T to reduce inference cost and time.
We detail the describer next in Sec. IV-A , followed by the assessor in Sec. IV-B . We provide a visual overview of D&A in Fig. 3 .

blocks.en:
Describing the full trajectory at once. In contrast to prior work [ 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 , 26 ] that predicts a single reward r t = R ( o 1 : t , l ) r_{t}=R(o_{1:t},l) causally and then iterates over t t to label dense rewards, D&A consumes the entire trajectory o 1 : T o_{1:T} in a single pass.
By describing the trajectory holistically, D D can place each timestep in the context of what happens before and after it, yielding descriptions that are temporally consistent.

blocks.en:
Grounding the description in scene entities. Withholding l l avoids confirmation bias but introduces a new failure mode: without any knowledge of the task, the describer may omit details that turn out to be critical for downstream assessment.
Take the example in Fig. 3 , where an entity extractor may describe the target book as “Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahnemann, “the book with an orange spine”, “the book with a pencil on the white cover”, etc. The entity should reflect the granularity in the instruction to avoid ambiguity in the description.
To resolve this without leaking l l into the describer, we decompose D D into two stages: an entity extractor E E that lists all scene entities e e , both task-relevant and task-irrelevant, from the instruction and video, and a grounded describer D desc D^{\text{desc}} that narrates the trajectory anchored to those entities: d 1 : T = D desc ( o 1 : T , E ( o 1 : T , l ) ) d_{1:T}=D^{\text{desc}}\big(o_{1:T},\,E(o_{1:T},l)\big) .
Since D desc D^{\text{desc}} does not know which entities are task-relevant, the full describer D D is effectively blind to l l .
Next, we describe how the description is used by the assessor.

blocks.en: IV-B Success Criteria Generation and Reward Assessment
blocks.zh: 四-B 成功标准制定和奖励评估

blocks.en:
Given the grounded description d d and instruction l l , the assessor’s role is to produce the per-timestep reward sequence r 1 : T r_{1:T} .
At this stage, one might again be tempted to naïvely query an LLM/VLM directly by giving it ( l , d ) (l,d) and asking it to score progress.
In practice, however, we find this naïve version fails in a characteristic way: the assessor frequently collapses to outputting all zeros (when it cannot tell whether meaningful progress has been made) or becomes a binary success detector and simply interpolates from 0 0 to 1 1 as shown in Fig. 1 .
However, to generate rewards useful for downstream applications, we would want them to encode much more granular progress information, e.g., partial progress towards task or subtask completions.
Such granular rewards would provide more useful, dense signals for policy learning, e.g., by improving the sample efficiency of reinforcement learning policies or by helping to filter out poor-quality actions in imitation learning [ 34 ] .

鉴于有依据的描述d和指令l,评估员的作用是制作每时一步的奖励序列r:Tr_{1:T}.

然而在实践中,我们发现这个天真版本以某种特征的方式失败:评估者经常崩溃,输出出所有零(当它无法判断是否取得了有意义的进展)或成为二进制成功探测器,并且简单地插出从0到1 1,如图1所示.
然而,为了产生对下游应用有用的奖励,我们希望它们编码出更多颗粒性进展信息,例如,在完成任务或完成次级任务方面取得部分进展。
这种颗粒式奖励将为政策学习提供更有用、更密集的信号,例如,通过提高强化学习政策的抽样效率或帮助过滤模仿学习中质量低下的行动[34]。

blocks.en:
Grounding the assessor in an explicit success criterion. This failure mode suggests the assessor lacks a clear target for progress: l l specifies what to do, but not necessarily what describes task success .
We address this by having the assessor first produce task completion explicitly. Concretely, given ( l , d 1 : T ) (l,d_{1:T}) , the assessor internally generates a natural-language success criterion c c —a description of the observable state of the world when l l has been fully accomplished—and then scores each timestep of the description against c c rather than against l l alone: r 1 : T = A ( l , d 1 : T ) = A score ( d 1 : T , C ( l , d 1 : T ) ) , r_{1:T}=A(l,\,d_{1:T})=A^{\text{score}}\big(d_{1:T},\,C(l,\,d_{1:T})\big), where C C generates the success criterion c c and A score A^{\text{score}} scores the description against it.
Anchoring assessment to c c reframes “estimate progress toward l l ” as the better-posed question “how close is d d to satisfying success criteria c c ?”, helping (1) admit a meaningful notion of partial progress and (2) resist both reward collapse modes.

blocks.en: IV-C From Progress to Rich Language Feedback
blocks.zh: 从进步到丰富语言反馈

blocks.en:
Scalar reward signals execution failure without offering actionable context for policy correction. By evaluating trajectory progress relative to defined success criteria, D&A constructs an implicit semantic rubric over time. Tracking criteria fulfillment across timesteps enables D&A to localize execution deviations, demonstrating an implicit understanding of how and why a trajectory failed.
To convert these diagnostic capabilities into downstream guidance, we augment the assessor A A with a feedback generator F ( l , d 1 : T ) F(l,d_{1:T}) that outputs a text string f f containing a failure analysis and corrective instructions. This updates the assessor formulation to: A ( l , d 1 : T ) = A score ( d 1 : T , C ( l , d 1 : T ) , F ( l , d 1 : T ) ) A(l,d_{1:T})=A^{\text{score}}\big(d_{1:T},C(l,d_{1:T}),F(l,d_{1:T})\big) .
See Fig. 3 for feedback examples.

blocks.en: IV-D Using D&A for Downstream Policy Improvement
blocks.zh: IV-D 利用D&A改进下游政策

blocks.en: The dense progress rewards and rich language feedback produced by D&A can be readily leveraged across various downstream policy improvement paradigms. Here we outline how D&A accelerates the paradigms used in our experiments in Sec. V , online and offline reinforcement learning (RL) and Code-as-Policies (CaP) [ 37 ] . Though we specifically detail those, D&A is a general-purpose reward and rich feedback framework and can be paired with other applications.
blocks.zh: 发展与援助所产生的密集进展回报和丰富的语言反馈,可以随时通过各种下游政策改进模式加以利用。 在此,我们概述了研发如何加快我们在Sec.V、在线和离线强化学习(RL)和Code-as-Polices(CaP)[37]的实验中使用的范式。 尽管我们具体详细介绍了这些内容,但开发与开发是一种通用的奖励和丰富的反馈框架,可以与其他应用程序相配合。

blocks.en: Online RL. In online RL, the agent improves its behavior through active interaction with the environment. Here, the absolute progress score r 1 : T = R ( o 1 : T , l ) r_{1:T}=R(o_{1:T},l) from D&A serves directly as the dense environment reward and can be optimized by any online RL algorithm. In our experiments, we fine-tune a frozen base policy with latent-space RL [ 38 ] .
blocks.zh: 在线 RL. 在在线RL中,代理通过与环境的积极互动来改善行为. 在此,来自D&A的绝对进取分数r : T = R (o 1: T, l) r_{ 1: T}= (o_{ 1: T}) 直接起到密集环境奖励的作用,可以通过任何在线RL算法来优化. 在我们的实验中,我们用潜入空间RL[38]微调了被冻结的基础政策.

blocks.en:
Offline RL. In offline RL, we are given a dataset 𝒟 = { τ n } n = 1 N \mathcal{D}=\{\tau_{n}\}_{n=1}^{N} of trajectories without ground-truth reward labels, and use D&A to supply the missing reward signal. Since D&A’s progress scores are bounded within [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] and reflect global task completion, we treat them as a potential function [ 39 ] , from which we derive per-timestep potential-based dense rewards r t r_{t} and, in turn, offline advantages: A t = r m ​ i ​ n ​ ( t + C , T ) − r t A_{t}=r_{min(t+C,T)}-r_{t} with action chunk size C C .
We use these advantages for filtering the training data or conditioning a policy on them (cf. RECAP and CFGRL [ 27 , 40 ] ); at test time, conditioning on a positive advantage biases generation towards optimal trajectories, maximizing downstream performance using D&A’s zero-shot rewards.
blocks.zh:
离线RL. 在离线RL中,我们得到一个数据集D={\\ n}n=1 N\mathcal{D}=\{\tau_{n=n=1}^{N}没有地-地-地-地奖励标签的轨迹,并使用D&A来提供缺失的奖励信号. 由于D&A的进步分数在[0, 1] [0, 1] 之内,并反映全球任务完成情况,因此我们将它们视为一种潜在的函数[39],我们从中得出了基于时间步的潜在密集奖励r t r r_{t] , 并由此获得离线优势: a t = r m i n (t + C, T ) – r r → r → min (t + C, T)} - r_{t ) 有动作块 C 大小 。
我们利用这些优势来过滤培训数据或制定相关政策(参见RECAP和CFGRL[27,40]);在测试时,以正面优势为条件产生出对最佳轨迹的偏差,利用研发的零射出回报来使下游业绩最大化。

blocks.en:
Code-as-Policies. Recent observations in robot failure analysis [ 41 ] and feedback-driven optimization [ 42 ] suggest that rich language feedback can improve policy performance.
We evaluate D&A as a between-attempt feedback source for an open-loop CaP planner. At every attempt, the planner observes the initial scene state and generates a code plan which is then executed open-loop in the environment. Across attempts, the planner keeps track of previous plans, and feedback generated by D&A which identifies the failure modes and proposes corrections.
blocks.zh:
暗号警察 机器人故障分析的最新观测[41]和反馈驱动优化[42]表明丰富的语言反馈可以提高政策性能.
我们评价D&A是一个开放的 CaP 规划器的尝试反馈源。 在每次尝试中,规划者都会观察初始场景状态,生成一个代码计划,然后在环境中执行开放. 通过各种尝试,规划者不断跟踪以往的计划,以及研发产生的反馈,这些反馈能够识别故障模式并提出更正。

blocks.en: We evaluate D&A against the six strongest-performing approaches, spanning both explicitly post-trained and zero-shot reward models to provide a comprehensive analysis of the current landscape. If not denoted otherwise, we choose Gemini 3 Flash as a base model for D&A to balance cost and performance, but also report benchmark numbers for GPT-6 Astra ( D&A ∗ ) to demonstrate capability scaling.
blocks.zh: 我们对照六种表现最强的方法来评估发展与评估,这些方法明确跨越经过培训后和零发奖赏模式,以全面分析目前的情况。 如果没有其他表示的话,我们选择双子座3 Flash作为D&A平衡成本和性能的基准模型,但也报告GPT-6 Astra(D&A *)的基准号,以显示能力缩放.

blocks.en: Post-trained Baselines are explicitly trained on robotics datasets to predict progress. The following approaches all use Qwen-3-VL [ 43 ] as the base model. RoboReward [ 15 ] fine-tunes to predict discrete end-of-episode scores from 1 to 5, trained on large-scale robotic data [ 44 , 45 ] augmented with counterfactual language instructions that simulate failed or mismatched trajectories. Robometer [ 16 ] fine-tunes on RBM-1M (optimal and suboptimal data) with a multi-objective framework that jointly predicts continuous progress in [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] , binary success, and pairwise trajectory preferences. SOLE-R1 [ 30 ] fine-tunes on CoT [ 36 ] and continuous progress estimates and then uses reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) to further tune the model.

Zero-shot Baselines leverage the world knowledge of off-the-shelf VLMs without any task- or robotics-specific fine-tuning. Naive VLM models the mapping R : ( o 1 : T , l ) ↦ r 1 : T R:(o_{1:T},\,l)\mapsto r_{1:T} with a single VLM call, predicting progress without decoupling or success-criteria reasoning. GVL [ 11 ] prompts a VLM with temporally shuffled frames, forcing it to judge each frame’s intrinsic progress independently of chronological order to counter the VLM’s bias toward time continuity. TOPReward [ 12 ] prompts a VLM with the full video and instruction and, rather than emitting progress as text, extracts it from the token logit of the “True” response to whether the instruction matches the execution.

blocks.en: (Q2) How well does D&A generalize to different tasks and embodiments?
blocks.zh: (问题2) 发展与投资在多大程度上将不同的任务和表现概括起来?

blocks.en:
To evaluate D&A across tasks, embodiments, and language, we evaluate on three offline benchmarks: D&A-Bench , a generalization benchmark we collected manually that is guaranteed to be out-of-distribution to all models to stress-test fine-grained scene and language understanding, and two external benchmarks RBM-EVAL-OOD [ 16 ] and RoboRewardBenchmark [ 15 ] .
We propose D&A-Bench to evaluate nuanced scene understanding (e.g., “dose exactly 16 g of coffee beans”), counting (“build a 5 block tower”), and semantic reasoning (“assemble the car”). The benchmark comprises 54 (27 success, 27 failure) trajectories over 14 YAM tasks each annotated with 10 VLM-generated paraphrases of the instruction to test language robustness. We report the Kendall τ α \tau_{\alpha} coefficient [ 49 ] for D&A-Bench and RBM-EVAL-OOD , measuring how well a reward model’s final-step prediction align with the ground-truth ordering of optimal, sub-optimal, and failure trajectories ( ∈ [ − 1 , + 1 ] \in[-1,+1] ; higher is better). RoboRewardBenchmark uses discrete end-of-episode progress labels reports Mean Absolute Error (MAE; lower is better).

Across all three benchmarks ( Fig. 5 ), D&A closes the gap to post-trained models, outperforming RoboReward on RBM-EVAL-OOD , Robometer on RoboRewardBenchmark , and SOLE-R1 on both. On D&A-Bench , D&A leverages the generalization and reasoning capabilities of its base VLM, scoring highest ( 0.67 0.67 ) and beating the best post-trained models Robometer ( 0.56 0.56 ) and RoboReward ( 0.43 0.43 ). Zero-shot TOPReward ( 0.24 0.24 ) and GVL ( 0.27 0.27 ) fail to generalize to those challenging tasks. D&A improves + 0.23 +0.23 over Naive VLM , which here is a surprisingly strong baseline: because the benchmark rewards scene and language generalization, even unstructured prompting of a strong base VLM generalizes far better than GVL and TOPReward , which cannot reliably compare trajectories. Fig. 7(b) illustrates this on “hit the enter key,” whose completion is only seen by a subtle on-screen change: D&A tracks the full trajectory and cleanly separates the success from a visually similar failure, whereas Robometer assigns the two nearly the same reward, RoboReward / SOLE-R1 score them oppositely, and zero-shot Naive VLM / GVL / TOPReward score both high. More qualitative examples in Sec. XIV .
Finally, we demonstrate the scalability of D&A by using GPT-6 Astra as a base model ( D&A ∗ ), achieving SOTA results on all three benchmarks.

blocks.en: (Q3) How does D&A scale with the underlying VLM?
blocks.zh: (问题3)D&A如何与基础VLM相适应?

blocks.en:
We investigate how D&A ’s ability to predict progress from video scales with base model capability. In Fig. 8 , we plot trajectory ranking performance (Kendall τ α \tau_{\alpha} on RBM-EVAL-OOD ) against the cost per million tokens, using cost as a proxy for model capability. Baselines are shown as dashed horizontal lines.
Across all base model families, we observe a clear upward trend: as D&A ’s base model capability increases, so does the ability to discriminate trajectory optimality. GVL also scales with the underlying model but at a much lower rate. TOPReward faces a major barrier on closed-source models through its reliance on token logprobs—which are unavailable for Gemini 3—and degrading performance under mandatory chat templates enforced by proprietary platforms. Our results further follow the negative scaling trend of TOPReward observed in the original publication [ 12 ] . D&A with Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-6 Astra as a base model achieves SOTA performance on the benchmark with 0.734 0.734 and 0.714 0.714 , validating the observed trend and efficacy of our approach.

blocks.en: VI Limitations and Discussion
blocks.zh: 六. 限制和讨论

blocks.en:
In this work, we introduce D&A, a methodology for leveraging frontier models in reward modeling and rich feedback. We counter confirmation bias and address hallucinated success by decoupling description and assessment. We demonstrate the efficacy of D&A on several real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
While effective, our approach introduces several limitations. First, it inherits the systemic constraints of off-the-shelf frontier models, including high inference latency, token cost, and restricted context windows. Because these models are typically accessed via closed-source APIs, they introduce stochasticity and limited granular control. They also remain susceptible to occasional semantic hallucinations, which can degrade description fidelity and subsequent reward assessment.
Second, the generated reward is bounded by the granularity of natural language descriptions. This poses challenges in domains requiring highly nuanced or continuous reward structures that are difficult to verbalize, such as precise spatial relationships or absolute geometric distances.
Despite these challenges, D&A marks a pivotal shift from fine-tuning to zero-shot robotics reward modeling that scales with rapid advances in frontier VLMs.

我们的做法虽然有效,但也提出了若干限制。 首先,它继承了现成的前沿模型的系统性制约,包括高推论延迟,象征性成本,和受限上下文窗口等. 因为这些模型一般通过闭源API访问,它们引入了分色和有限的颗粒控制. 它们也仍然容易受到不定期的语义幻觉的影响,这种幻觉可以降低描述的忠诚度并导致奖励评估。

Rubric for End - of - Episode Progress : * 1 - No Success : The final state shows no goal - relevant change for the command . * 2 - Minimal Progress : The final state shows a small but insufficient change toward the goal . * 3 - Partial Completion : The final state shows good progress toward the goal but violates more than one requirement or a major requirement . * 4 - Near Completion : The final state is correct in region and intent but misses a single minor requirement . * 5 - Perfect Completion : The final state visibly satisfies all requirements . Hints & Clarifications for Scoring ( Particularly 3 vs . 4): To correctly distinguish between a Partial Completion (3) and a Near Completion (4), you must differentiate between MAJOR and MINOR task requirements based on the following rules : * Treat a requirement as MAJOR when the PRIMARY object identity or the PRIMARY spatial relation to the reference object is not satisfied . If a major requirement is missed , the score must be 3 or lower . * Treat a requirement as MINOR when the PRIMARY object identity and PRIMARY spatial relation to the reference object are satisfied , but an AUXILIARY constraint is missed ( e . g ., the orientation of the object is slightly off , or the object is placed a bit too far forward / backward but still in the correct general region ). Missing a single minor requirement results in a score of 4. Provide a brief step - by - step reasoning analyzing the observation against the rubric and hints . Conclude with your final discrete score in the following JSON format : [ {{ "score" : int }} ]

blocks.en: ⬇ Task : "{{task}}" Scene descriptions : {{ description }} 1. The task text fixes which objects count ( category , color , shape , and wording ). Scene descriptions are the only evidence of what is in the environment . Do not "ground" the task by renaming scene objects to match the task . 2. For each object the task requires , it may be tied only to scene mentions that refer to that same entity without contradiction . Do not substitute a different object because it could serve the same role . If attributes in the scene conflict with the task ’s description of that object, or no clear referent exists, treat that requirement as absent. 3. You may align short paraphrases across timesteps only when they plainly denote the same physical object already present in the scene-not to map task nouns onto other objects. 4. If ALL required objects are absent by these rules, the task cannot be completed in this scene: use all 0% progress and explain in "completion state". Otherwise define precisely what the environment would look like if the task were FULLY and COMPLETELY finished (not started, not halfway-entirely done). Reward partial progress if the task is only partially completed and some required objects are present. 5. For each timestep, reason about the % progress towards that fully completed state. 6. Progress is defined as % progress towards the fully completed state. Progress does not have to be monotonic, i.e., the robot can reverse progress. 7. If the task was not fully completed, describe the failure. 8. If the task was not fully completed, give feedback on what the robot should have done differently. Respond with a list of progress values (ordered by frame) in the following JSON format: [ {{ "failure": str, "feedback": str, "completion state": str, "progress": [int, int, ...] }} ] Before you respond, reflect whether the task is actually fully completed, otherwise adjust the progress values!’
blocks.zh: 任务 : “ 任务 ” 场景描述: {{ 描述: }}. 1. 任务文本确定哪些对象可以计数(类别、颜色、形状和措辞)。 场景描述是环境里唯一的证据。 通过重命名场景对象来匹配任务, 不要“ 打开” 任务 。 2. 对于任务要求的每个物体,它可能仅与提及同一实体的场景有关,没有矛盾。 不要取而代之,因为它可以发挥同样的作用。 如果场景中的属性与任务对该物体的描述相冲突,或者不存在明确的参考,则将这一要求视为不存在。 3. 只有当简略的句子明确表示在现场已经存在的同一物理对象时,才能将任务名词映射到其他对象上。 4. 如果这些规则没有列出所有所需的对象,则无法在此场景中完成任务:使用所有0%的进度,并在"完成状态"中解释. 否则,就确切地界定如果任务全面完成(没有开始,没有完成一半),环境将是什么样子。 如果任务仅部分完成,并存在一些必要的对象,则奖励部分进展。 5. 每一步,说明在实现完全完成状态方面的百分比进展的原因。 6. 进展的定义是完全完成状态的进展百分比。 进步不必是单调的,即机器人可以逆转进步. 7. 如果任务没有完全完成,请说明失败情况。 8. 如果任务没有完全完成,请反馈机器人本应如何做。 以以下 JSON 格式的进度值列表(按帧排列)响应: [QQ"失败":str,"feedback":str,"完成状态":str,"进步": [int,int,.]_.] 在回复之前,请反映任务是否真的完全完成,否则会调整进度值!
